resources.string: Engaged — Godwall holds the VPN slot
Stood down — nothing is being filtered

Godwall filters DNS: it decides which names resolve, for which app, over an encrypted upstream. It is not a packet firewall on its own — an app denied here can still reach an address it already knows. Packet-level denial needs the privileged shell from Yojimbo, and the enforcement badge below says whether one is in force.
Battery saver. Name lookups are filtered and encrypted; no per-app network denial is applied.
Per-app network denial through the platform firewall chain. Name lookups still go to your configured upstream but are not filtered by name.
The default. Name filtering and per-app network denial together.
The slot carries Godwall\'s own tailnet node and nothing else. Names are not filtered while this mode is selected.
Name filtering, per-app network denial, and the tailnet node, all inside the one slot.
Applied to the next lookup — the engine keeps the slot, so nothing reconnects.
Saved. It takes effect when you engage.
This mode asks for a tier this device cannot run — see the banner above.
Pinned to %1$s, which is not available right now — %2$s is carrying enforcement instead.

Which mechanism actually carries out per-app denial. Each row below was probed on this device just now — an unavailable backend says why, and pinning one that is unavailable does not silently become the pin.
Walks iptables → ConnectivityManager → NetworkPolicyManager → VPN → Proxy and takes the first that answered.
The donor apps call these Root mode, VPN mode and Proxy mode. They are the same choice as the rows above: Root mode is iptables, VPN mode is Godwall\'s own tunnel, Proxy mode is the egress chain.
%1$d blocked · %2$d name-isolated · %3$d excluded from the tunnel · %4$d refused
Operating normally. Nothing is claiming a state it cannot reach.
The engine failed to start: %1$s Nothing is being filtered.
Another app is holding a VPN on this device. While it does, Godwall cannot take the slot and filters nothing.
Some lookups are going to a resolver Godwall does not see. Open the DNS card for the addresses.
%1$d stored rule(s) name Godwall itself. They are refused rather than applied — cutting Godwall off would take the filter down with it.
This mode asks for per-app network denial, which needs the privileged shell from Yojimbo. Until one is attached, only name-based denial is in force.
This mode asks for the tailnet node, and the mesh data plane is not in this build. No tunnel is running.
%1$d denial(s) you set cannot be applied: they name core networking or a VPN provider, and applying them could take this device off the network.
This device trusts %1$d certificate authority you or an administrator installed. Any holder of one can read TLS from apps that trust user CAs. Godwall\'s own upstream never does.
The name filter is on but no domains are loaded, so nothing is being blocked by list.
Protection is paused. Every name resolves normally until the countdown ends.
Lockdown is on: every name lookup that reaches Godwall is answered with the block response.
Child lock is on. The engine keeps running; the controls stay frozen until the PIN is entered.
Keeps the slot and the tunnel; stops applying every name rule for the countdown, then resumes on its own.
Nothing to pause — Godwall is not engaged.

Answers every name lookup that reaches Godwall with the block response, in every mode. Apps you excluded from the tunnel are unaffected — their traffic never enters it. An app that already knows an address can still reach it.
Godwall is not engaged, so no lookup reaches it and this changes nothing yet. It applies the moment you engage.
Always-on VPN is on, and connections without a VPN are blocked.
Always-on VPN is on, but connections without a VPN are still allowed.
Always-on VPN is off for this device.
Android only reports this to a running VPN service. Engage Godwall once and it will be read.
Android owns this switch — no app can set it. This opens the system screen where it lives.
This device has no system VPN settings screen to open.
Sends real traffic and reports what came back — the slot, the upstream, the filter, the leak check, the chain and the enforcement backend.
On — controls are frozen until the PIN is entered
Freezes the master switch, the mode, lockdown and pause. The engine keeps doing whatever it was already doing — a lock that stopped protection would be a way to turn protection off without the PIN.
A PIN must be at least %1$d characters.
Child lock is on — enter the PIN to use this control.
Tor is not in this build: it needs the tor binary and its config tree, which are a separate payload this build was not given. Nothing Tor-related is running, and no control here pretends otherwise.
I2P is not in this build: it needs the i2pd binary and i2pd.conf, which are a separate payload this build was not given.

Local dnscrypt-proxy is not in this build: it needs the dnscrypt-proxy binary and its .toml, which are a separate payload this build was not given. DoT and DoH upstreams are unaffected and are what the DNS card reports.
Hotspot sharing is not in this build: routing tethered clients through the tunnel is done with iptables rules through a bundled busybox, which is a separate payload this build was not given.
Search covers apps, UIDs and rules, which live on the Wardens and Firewall screens. It is not on this screen because there is nothing here it could search.
